findings.text: The hrtimer cancellation interface allows lock free observation of activity plus an attempt to withdraw a queued timer plus a wait for completion of a running soft callback. Inactive timers are reported as idle, running callbacks are reported as busy, and successfully withdrawn timers trigger cancellation tracing.

The alarm control interface allows attempting cancellation of an alarm with automatic dequeue on success, plus repeated cancellation until the timer is no longer running, plus advancing a periodic alarm past a reference time while counting missed periods, plus a convenience form that uses the current time of the owning base.

The supporting time interface allows queueing a posix timer signal with status derived from the interval, plus copying a remaining time to user space, plus translating a restart block sleep type into the appropriate user copy with fault and restart signalling, plus releasing debug state for an on stack timer, plus observing whether the per CPU tick is marked stopped.

Queue occupancy is tracked per clock index with a bitmask of active clocks and a next expiry per clock. Enqueue marks the clock active and refreshes the next expiry when the new timer becomes earliest. Removal clears the active mark when the queue empties and refreshes the next expiry when the earliest timer leaves.

The queued flag uses ordered publication so that unlocked observers see a consistent state. Activation publishes the enqueued state before linking, deactivation publishes the new state before unlinking, and requeue republishes the enqueued state around the queue update.

Timer placement prefers the local CPU when suitable and otherwise selects among online housekeeping capable targets with awareness of tickless operation and pinning. Suitability accepts any local target and any target when the local CPU is offline, and otherwise requires the adjusted expiry to be no earlier than the next event already scheduled on the candidate.

Expiry updates may stay linked when order is preserved. An update that would move past the successor requires requeue, an update to the earliest position may stay linked, and any other update may stay linked only when it does not move ahead of the predecessor.
Low resolution builds extend relative timeouts by the nominal timer granularity and record whether the original mode was relative, while other builds pass the requested time through unchanged.

Callback time and alarm type derive from clock identity. Monotonic and realtime and boottime and TAI clocks each map to a matching time source with monotonic fallback and diagnostic on unexpected identity. Realtime alarm clocks map to realtime alarms and other alarm clocks map to boottime alarms with diagnostic on unexpected identity.

Periodic alarm advancement moves the stored expiry forward by whole intervals until it passes the reference time and reports how many periods elapsed. A large lag uses division to skip multiple periods with correction for exact alignment, while a small lag steps by a single interval. Rearm accumulates missed periods into overrun accounting and restarts the alarm.

Freezer deadline tracking retains the earliest requested absolute expiry among realtime and boottime alarms. Each request maps to its freezer counterpart, computes remaining duration against current base time, and under lock keeps the smallest delta with its expiry and type. Unexpected types trigger diagnostic and leave state unchanged.

User timer validation compares soft expiry adjusted by base offset against scheduled and current time. Timers that are not earliest or that remain in the future are accepted. Expired earliest timers are withdrawn without reprogramming, marked inactive, traced as expired, and reported as not acceptable.

Alarm clock operations require a real time clock device and privileged creation. Resolution and time queries report invalid argument failure without a device. Creation reports operation not supported failure without a device and permission failure without wake alarm privilege, then maps the clock and initializes the alarm with its handler.

Activation and deactivation emit debug and trace hooks. Start paths activate debug state and trace start with mode and prior armed state. Removal paths deactivate debug state. Cancel and expired paths emit dedicated trace events. Debug builds perform object tracking while minimal builds provide empty hooks with identical call sites.

Queue mutation requires holding the CPU base lock. Enqueue and removal and internal removal and same base requeue all assert lock ownership. Base next refresh and active mark updates occur only under this lock, which also protects against observing transient ordering violations during key updates.

Cross CPU migration hands over locks in a defined order. The old lock is released only after publishing an intermediate migration marker, the new lock is acquired before validating suitability, and on validation failure the locks and base are restored before retrying locally. Single CPU builds skip migration and retain the original base.

Alarm and posix and freezer state each have dedicated guarding. Alarm cancel holds the alarm base lock across timer cancel and dequeue. Alarm expiry handling and posix signal queueing hold the posix timer lock. Freezer updates hold the freezer delta lock across comparison and retention.

Lock free activity checks and soft callback waits use sequence and waiter coordination. Activity observation retries on sequence change or base change and reports queued or running state. Cancel waiting relaxes for hard context or migration base and otherwise accounts as a waiter while briefly holding the soft expiry lock to synchronize with soft interrupt expiry.

The timer object carries queue membership and mode and callback context. Observed members include is_queued and is_rel and is_soft and is_lazy and base and node, where node carries expires and soft expiry. Expiry setters accept absolute time with slack range.

The clock base links a CPU base with ordering and timing state. Observed clock members include index and offset and active and expires_next and running and seq and cpu_base. Observed CPU members include clock_base and lock and active_bases and online and expires_next and next_timer and deferred_rearm and deferred_needs_update and softirq_expiry_lock and timer_waiters. A global migration base serves as transient owner during handover.

The alarm object pairs an hrtimer with queue and type state. Observed alarm members include timer and node and type and data. Observed base members include lock and get_ktime and get_timespec. Observed posix members include it_lock and it_interval and it_overrun and it_status and it_clock and restart_block, where restart state carries nanosleep with sleep type and return pointers.

Tick scheduling state carries flags tested for stopped condition. Time values use second and nanosecond pairs in both kernel and user layouts. Observed members include flags and tv_sec and tv_nsec and nanosleep and type and rmtp and compat_rmtp, where sleep type selects native or compat copy out behavior.

Timer lifecycle moves among idle and queued and running with a transient migration owner. Enqueue publishes queued state and links the timer. Active checks report queued or running. Removal unlinks and publishes idle state. Migration uses a dedicated base between locks. Running callbacks pin the timer and forbid relocation.

Alarm cancellation retries until the timer is no longer reported busy. Each attempt tries timer cancellation under guard and dequeues on success. Busy reports trigger a wait for running completion before retrying. Posix wrappers delegate both the try step and the wait step to the underlying alarm primitives.

Interruptible alarm sleep arms and waits and cancels in a loop. The sleeper records itself as callback data, arms the alarm, sleeps while data remains, cancels on wake, and repeats while data persists without pending signals. Completion destroys on stack state, handles freezer retention when freezing, and either reports success or copies remaining time for restart.

Posix alarm arming converts relative requests to absolute base time and supports a signal free shortcut that only records expiry while reporting success. Creation gates on device presence and privilege before initializing. Rearm advances expiry and accumulates overruns before restarting.

Alarm expiry dispatch extracts the enclosing posix timer from the alarm and under lock queues its signal. Signal queueing validates the timer, derives status from whether an interval remains, and emits the pending notification.
Sleep wakeup clears the recorded sleeper and wakes its task when present. The handler receives the alarm and current time but acts only on stored task data, leaving absent sleepers untouched.

The alarm posix operation set exposes rearm and forward and remaining and cancel and wait and arm and create plus resolution and time queries. Each operation delegates to core alarm or hrtimer primitives with appropriate base selection and error signalling for missing device or privilege.

Expiry key mutation while linked can briefly violate queue order. The implementation performs the mutation only under the CPU base lock where no concurrent queue operation can observe the transient state, and either confirms order preservation via adjacent entry checks or unlinks without consulting the mutated key before reinsertion.

Removal location affects device reprogramming. Local removal of the earliest non lazy timer forces reprogramming unless deferred handling is active, in which case an update flag is set. Remote removal skips device access and relies on the remote interrupt to reprogram. Non earliest removals only refresh base next state.

Callback execution forbids relocation. Migration checks for running state and retains the original base when the timer is executing. Locality preference likewise retains the base for running timers regardless of tick or housekeeping considerations.

Unexpected clock and alarm identities are handled with fallback and diagnostic. Invalid callback clocks fall back to monotonic time. Unexpected alarm clocks fall back to boottime type. Invalid freezer types trigger diagnostic and abort without touching freezer state.

User visible sleep remainder handling can fail or restart. Copy out to native or compat pointers reports fault failure on bad addresses and otherwise requests restart. Sleep completion reports success on wake, success on elapsed remainder, restart with remainder when a sleep type persists, and freeze retention when freezing.
Empty queue is represented by a maximum time sentinel stored as the next expiry of the clock base. Base refresh selects the earliest linked expiry when occupied and otherwise stores KTIME_MAX.

Missing device and privilege and addressing outcomes use standard negative errors. Resolution and time queries report EINVAL without a device. Creation reports EOPNOTSUPP without a device and EPERM without privilege. Remainder copy reports EFAULT on bad user memory and ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK for restartable sleeps.

Queue and posix lifecycle states use distinct symbolic values. Timers publish HRTIMER_STATE_ENQUEUED on activation and HRTIMER_STATE_INACTIVE on withdrawal. Posix signal queueing selects POSIX_TIMER_REQUEUE_PENDING when an interval remains and POSIX_TIMER_DISARMED otherwise. Relative mode is indicated by HRTIMER_MODE_REL.
